text_read: Read in full: Chapter 4 'The Four Visions and the Meaning of Vitality' (source lines 3030-3646), Chapter 5 'The Preliminary Practices and the Domestication of Vitality' (3648-4275), Chapter 6 opening with 'The Six Key Points' (4277-4430). Read in part: Introduction opening (328-364); Ch. 6 on the light channels (4484-4512, 4600-4625, 4736-4770); Ch. 7 on Longchenpa's softening of the eye-pressing instruction (5360-5400); Ch. 8 on Thogal versus Trekcho and the crystal and eye-pressing introductions (6030-6200); Ch. 9 crystal-glasses introduction (6455-6490); endnotes carrying the Tibetan for the first-vision list, the eye-pressing lines, dark retreat sources, and the Bon postures and gazes (8834-8858, 9151-9165, 9444-9469). Parts I and most of III (historical argument) were located by keyword search only and not read.
mode_evidence: The lights are seen by the eyes against the sky or in a dark room. Longchenpa (Treasury of Words and Meanings) contrasts Thogal with Trekcho precisely on this point: wisdom is 'directly seen', it 'shines forth from the eyes', and seeing is 'through the faculties, independent of the words of mental analysis'. The Tantra of Unimpeded Sound: 'wisdom's key point is that it emerges from the eyes'. The opening description says the mandala finally appears 'without the slightest effort of active visualization'. Geisshuesler himself compares the first lights to entoptic floaters and ganzfeld imagery.
onset_evidence: Explicit induction for the person who sees nothing. (1) Treasury of Words and Meanings 283.3: at the very start of actual Thogal, press the eyeballs using two fingers rather than three to give rise to appearances; after three or four days phenomena arise without any pressure (Tibetan in endnote: zhag gsum bzhi na ma ltems kyang snang). (2) Longchenpa repeatedly: if struggling to make the visions arise naturally, begin by pressing on the vitality-channel [srog rtsa], which the book identifies with the aorta (elsewhere the spinal cord); Mirror of the Heart of Vajrasattva 334.1: turn the eyes up to the sky and press this channel and the sky fills with luminous appearances. (3) The Absence of Letters Tantra says press the eyes 'firmly' [rab tu] for the linked sheep; Longchenpa rewrites this as a 'slight' pressing while gazing to the side. (4) Prerequisites: the rushen preliminaries of body, speech and mind done to exhaustion, then settling into naturalness. (5) The lights do not appear at once because they are obstructed in the body; the seal of the heart must be 'torn open'. No statement that light comes only by grace. Time scales: three or four days for the pressure-free onset; forty-nine days as the standard dark retreat. Development: stabilising the chains within the blue expanse, then the four visions.

conditions.posture: Three postures: lion [seng ge], elephant [glang chen], sage [drang srong]; body and limbs completely still. Endnote, from the Bon Zhangzhung Nyengyu via Reynolds: five postures (dignified lion sitting like a dog on its haunches; reclining elephant on the belly; crouching ascetic; waddling goose; crystal antelope, the hardest).
conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: Key point of the gates [sgo'i gnad]: three gazes, upward, downward and sideways, pupils immobile and steady. Bon list of five gazes: upward (Dharmakaya), straight ahead (Sambhogakaya), downward (Nirmanakaya), right (Skilful Means), left (Discriminating Wisdom). Eyes unwavering and mind undistracted.
conditions.setting: Cloudless open sky; also the rays of the sun, a lamp, a reflective pool or a crystal; or a completely dark chamber [mun khang] for dark retreat [mun mtshams], also called the night-time practice.
conditions.duration_and_schedule: Eye pressure for the first three or four days only. Dark retreat standard length forty-nine days; some masters reported as spending years. No daily schedule given.
conditions.prerequisites: Nyingthig preliminaries: yoga of the sounds of the four elements; khordé rushen ['khor 'das ru shan] of body (run, shake, whirl, roll the head, act out the six classes of beings), speech (talk like a lunatic, shout phat, cry like animals until exhausted, then silence) and mind (act out thoughts and emotions); then the body-speech-mind preliminaries. The practice is described as the tradition's most secret.
conditions.other: Key point of the wind [rlung gi gnad]: breathe slowly and naturally through the mouth without altering it; Longchenpa adds the winds 'remain still' in three ways (not going out, not filling up inside, not coming and going). Speech: complete silence, 'like a mute'.

stages.label: vision of reality's immediacy [chos nyid mngon sum gyi snang ba]
stages.description: First something like smoke, then white wafting clouds, mirages, stars, fire sparks, butter lamps, and a great pervading blue; eventually light rays, seminal nuclei [thig le] and empty forms. Low intensity, much movement: the nuclei are 'minute and linked', fluttering, appearing and vanishing; they steady only after extended practice.

stages.label: vision of the intensification of experience [nyams gong 'phel gyi snang ba]
stages.description: Light intensifies and balances into five colours; nuclei grow in number and size; linked vajra sheep [rdo rje lu gu rgyud], like strings of pearls, appear within the nuclei; also cloudbanks, lattices, checkered forms, vertical lines, wheels, round rainbows, lotuses, fireflies, stupas. Still fluctuating.

stages.label: vision of awareness reaching its limit [rig pa tshad phebs kyi snang ba]
stages.description: Nuclei and chains 'mature into spiritual bodies'. Longchenpa's six steps: half a Buddha body, single bodies, Buddha with consort, five Buddhas with retinues, the five in a mandala, the great mandala of the hundred peaceful and wrathful deities.

stages.label: fourth vision
stages.description: All manifestation dissolves back into the expanse. Named only as the dissolution; not described in detail in the chapters read.

what_to_do_with_light: Stabilise and contain. Keep eyes unwavering and mind undistracted; when the blue expanse [dbyings] appears together with the linked sheep, subdue the chains so they do not flutter and hold them inside the enclosure of the expanse (Treasury of Words and Meanings 377.4). Blazing Lamp Tantra: place the chains in the 'prison of the expanse', without grasping. Do not separate from the appearances; remaining so, the four visions reach their full measure. Movement and conceptual reifying are the fault; control channels and winds to cut it.
obstacles_and_fixes: Nothing appears at first, because the energy is obstructed in the body: press the eyeballs with two fingers for the first days; or turn the eyes up to the sky and press the vitality-channel.
Chains and nuclei flutter, come and go: their movement is due to the five winds; keep the eyes and pupils unmoving, breathe gently through the mouth, and hold the chains within the blue expanse.
Dull, bound energy: the rushen preliminaries, done to exhaustion and followed by resting in naturalness [rnal du dbab], are what rouse it.
Conceptual movement during practice accumulates karma: cut it by controlling the key points of channels and winds.
cautions: Longchenpa softens the older tantra's 'press the eyes firmly' to a 'slight' pressing while gazing to the side.
The author notes Thogal is the tradition's most secret practice and that publishing these instructions raises an ethical issue of secrecy.
Aim is realisation of the nature of the experiences, not more experiences (Gyatso, cited).
interpretation: The lights are awareness [rig pa] residing in the heart, travelling through light channels (the kati crystal tube from heart to eyes) and issuing out through the eyes onto the sky; the thig le are both drops of energy in the body and specks in the visual field. Geisshuesler's own reading adds entoptic phenomena, sensory deprivation and culturally shaped meaning-making.
practice_summary: Prepare with the rushen preliminaries: move, shout and act out every impulse until exhausted, then rest in silence and stillness. For the main practice take a lion, elephant or sage posture and keep body and limbs motionless; stay silent; breathe slowly and naturally through the mouth. Fix the gaze upward, downward or sideways with the pupils steady, on a cloudless sky (the texts also name the sun's rays, a lamp, a pool, a crystal, or a fully dark room). If nothing appears, press the eyeballs with two fingers, Longchenpa says only slightly and while gazing sideways; after three or four days appearances come without pressure. Alternatively turn the eyes skyward and press the vitality-channel. Expect smoke, cloud, mirage, stars, sparks, lamp-like lights and a pervading blue, then restless specks and pearl-like chains. Hold eyes and mind unmoving and keep the chains inside the blue field until they steady; they then multiply, take five colours, and later form Buddha figures and mandalas.

key_passages.anchor: “press the eyeballs, using only two fingers rather than three” in order to give rise
key_passages.paraphrase: At the first moments of actual Thogal the practitioner presses the eyeballs with two fingers, not three, to bring on visual appearances; after three or four days they arise without pressure. The endnote gives the Tibetan and parallel places in the Treasury of the Supreme Vehicle I 407.5-6 and Bima Nyingthig I 373.1.

key_passages.paraphrase: For someone struggling to make the visions arise naturally, Longchenpa says to start by pressing the vitality-channel, which the book identifies with the aorta. The tantra: turn the eyes up to the sky, press this channel, and the sky fills with luminous appearances. The source does not say where on the body the pressure is applied.

key_passages.paraphrase: The first vision: one sees something like smoke, then white drifting cloud, mirage, stars, fire sparks, butter lamps and a great pervading blue; then rays, thig le and empty forms. The specks are small, linked and restless, steadying only after long practice.

key_passages.paraphrase: Key point of awareness: eyes unwavering, mind undistracted. When the blue expanse and the linked sheep dawn together, subdue the chains so they stop fluttering and hold them inside the enclosure of the expanse.

key_passages.paraphrase: The older tantra says to press the eyes firmly [rab tu] to bring on the linked sheep; Longchenpa gives it as a slight pressing of the eyes while gazing to the side, as the 'placement of awareness'.

key_passages.paraphrase: In Thogal the linked chains are seen nakedly in vision through the brightness of the light channels; conceptual thought stops at once. Wisdom is directly seen by the sense faculty, not sought through mental analysis.

new_leads: Longchenpa, Tshig don mdzod ch. 8 (pp. 271-284, 373-407 of the edition cited) and Theg mchog mdzod: the full Thogal instructions excerpted here; Germano 1992 dissertation translates much of it.
Longchenpa's two Nyingthig dark-retreat texts named in the endnote: nyin mtshan 'od kyi 'khor lo and rgya mtsho ar gtad kyi mun khrid 'od gsal 'khor lo.

Mirror of the Heart of Vajrasattva [rDo rje sems dpa' snying gi me long] and Tantra of the Introductions [Ngo sprod spras pa]: introductions by crystal held to a window, eye pressing ('thig le like fish-eyes'), crystal lenses over the eyes while sky gazing.
Reynolds 2011 (Zhangzhung Nyengyu five postures and gazes); Wangyal 2000 (dark retreat, nuclei like quicksilver); Hatchell 2014, Naked Seeing.
confidence_note: Academic conduit: passages are the author's translations and paraphrases of Longchenpa and the Seventeen Tantras, fragmentary and selected to serve a historical argument, so sequence and context of the originals are not preserved. Posture and gaze details are thin; the five-posture and five-gaze lists come from a Bon source at third hand (Reynolds). 'stimulus_independence: yes' rests on the three-or-four-days statement about eye pressure and on dark retreat; the sky or lamp remains as a visual ground in daytime practice. The candidate summary's 'where the classical texts treat dark retreat' is only an endnote list of titles. OCR renders Togal as 'Tégal' in places.
